# Coverage Report

**Generated:** 2026-10-01 (figures refreshed; disposition audit `CORR-COV-016`)
**Baseline:** BAS-REF-001 — source pinned to commit `308028fb` (v1.11.0), corpus authored at `2a408d5`
**Profiles:** `synthetic_reference` (primary), `as_is` (comparison)
**Machine-readable sibling:** `coverage-report.json` (regenerated by
`python3 docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py coverage`)

> states structural mapping coverage only. It asserts **no ISO 26262
> conformity**, no ASIL capability, no IEC 61508 conformity, no certification,
> no tool qualification and no ASPICE capability level. All 263 indexed records
> are `human_approval_status: pending` and `production_authorized: false`.

`source_grounding` detail, verbatim from the tool: *99/263 - artifacts with
source_refs (101 anchors available)*. The 164 records without `source_refs` are
overwhelmingly synthetic, which is expected — a synthetic record has nothing in
the pinned source to point at.

`automated_review_coverage` detail, verbatim from the tool: *144/224 artifacts
covered by 15 review records; reviewed_by links consistent with reviewed_ids*.
The denominator is 224 rather than 263 because it counts distinct artifact
**IDs** across both profiles, and 39 IDs exist in both `as_is` and
`synthetic_reference` by design.

`actual_product_evidence` detail, verbatim from the tool: *0 target-hardware
executions: execution_kind has no target-hardware member, so none can be claimed
(blocked, not fabricated); of 44 execution records: 15 host/simulation (real
product code, not target hardware), 29 synthetic_fixture/none, 0 undeclared.*

**Two cautions on this table.** First, it is hand-authored, so it can drift; the
live figures are `coverage-report.json` and the `coverage` command's own output,
and every figure above was taken from a run on 2026-10-01. The version this
report replaces carried figures from before the corpus expanded and several were
stale; they were corrected here rather than left to be discovered. Second, five
dimensions here are presence checks or declared constants rather than
measurements — `scope_accounting` and `export_reproducibility` (presence),
`semantic_consistency_checks` (a declared count of check categories) and
`human_approval` / `production_authorization` (policy constants enforced by other
rules and by gate `[7/8]`). The generated traceability document labels each one;
none keys off an acceptance gate.

## 2. Population Counts — and Why There Are Three of Them

A reader comparing these will otherwise conclude one is wrong. All three are
correct and measure different things. **They are not harmonised, on purpose.**

| Count | Tool that produces it | What it measures | Arithmetic |
|---|---|---|---|
| **286** | `validate` | schema-validated artefact **files** carrying an `id` | 263 corpus records + 23 scenario records |
| **263** | `load_artifact_index` | unique `(profile, id)` records | 267 corpus JSON files walked; 263 carry an `id`; all 263 `(profile, id)` pairs unique |
| **224** | `automated_review_coverage` | distinct artifact **IDs** across both profiles | 263 − 39 ids that exist in both profiles |

Why 286 > 263: the 23 records under `scenarios/` carry an `id` but no `profile`,
so they are not profile-scoped records and are not in the artifact index.
`validate` walks `corpus/` and `scenarios/`; the index walks `corpus/` only.

Why 286 = 263 + 23, and why `iter_corpus_artifacts` yields 267 files for 263
records: **4** of the 267 are registry/aggregate containers with no `id` —
`corpus/synthetic_reference/shared/assumption-registry.json`, the sibling
`parameter-registry.json`, and the two link-registry files under
`corpus/synthetic_reference/traceability/`. `validate` skips those explicitly
(`if "id" not in d: continue  # registry container files`). The former
`FB2-REV-000001` duplicate that made this arithmetic lossy has been removed:
**all 263 `(profile, id)` pairs are now unique**, so the index collapses
nothing.

Why 263 > 224: **39** IDs exist in both `as_is` and `synthetic_reference`. That
is the corpus's profile-isolation design decision, not duplication. The 39 are
`FB2-HW-TSR-000001..000003`, `FB2-SAF-FSR-000001..000003`,
`FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001`, `FB2-SAF-SGO-000001`, `FB2-SW-DSN-000001..000003`,
`FB2-SW-IMP-000001..000004`, `FB2-SW-SWR-000001..000003`,
`FB2-VER-EXE-000001..000016` and `FB2-VER-TMS-000001..000005`.

### 3.1 `standards_mapping` — the number that rose, and why

`standards_mapping` moved **16/38 → 33/38** in this pass. That is not an
improvement in the corpus; it is a consequence of how the dimension is measured
and of doing the work the audit demanded.

The dimension asks: *does the text that claims a disposition name at least one
artefact identifier that resolves?* `CORR-COV-016` rewrote every disposition to
name the record it rests on and the specific family that is missing — which is
what recording the evidence for a decision means — so 17 further entries became
"backed".

The figure that reflects substance went the other way:

| Tally | Before (2026-09-29) | After (2026-10-01) |
|---|---|---|
| ASPICE, 28 applicable — `mapped` | 12 | **4** |
| ASPICE — `partially_mapped` | 10 | **21** |
| ASPICE — `gap` | 6 | **3** |
| ISO 26262, 10 applicable — `mapped` | 6 | **0** |
| ISO — `partially_mapped` | 2 | **8** |
| ISO — `referenced` | 2 | 2 |
| `standards_mapping` (by backing) | 16/38 | 33/38 |

The three remaining unbacked ASPICE entries are `SWE.3`, `HWE.3` and `HWE.4` —
the three processes **no artefact in the corpus references at all**. The two
unbacked ISO entries are `part_1_vocabulary` and `part_10_guidelines`, both
`referenced` and unchanged. The per-process evidence is in
`governance/coverage-plan.json` under `CORR-COV-016` and in each entry's
`disposition` and `disposition_reason`.

By review state: reviewed 414, pending 75.

> **Link currency is not maintained, and this is measured, not suspected.**
> Every link carries both endpoint revisions. Comparing each link's recorded
> endpoint revision against the endpoint artefact's current revision:
> **326 of 489 links differ, and all 489 carry `change_suspect_status: false`.**
> So the corpus holds 326 links whose recorded endpoint revision is stale and
> marks none of them suspect. Link *resolution* is verified on every run; link
> *currency* is not. This is the specific shortfall behind `SUP.11
> Traceability Management` being `partially_mapped`.

Note on the registry files, measured: four registry files hold 540 links in
total and de-duplicate to 489.

| Registry file | Links |
|---|---:|
| `traceability/link-registry/as_is/links-cell-voltage.json` | 117 |
| `traceability/link-registry/synthetic_reference/links-cell-voltage.json` | 195 |
| `corpus/synthetic_reference/traceability/link-registry/synthetic_reference/links-cell-voltage.json` | 51 — **a strict subset of the 195 above**; redundant |
| `corpus/synthetic_reference/traceability/link-registry/synthetic_reference/links-concept-lifecycle.json` | 177 — **the only copy**, and load-bearing |

The 51-link redundant copy is left in place and reported rather than deleted. The
177-link concept-lifecycle file is **not** redundant: the canonical tree has no
counterpart for it, so removing it would delete 177 links. The earlier
description of this layout as "51 of 172 links" understated it and called both
files redundant.

## 5. Source Inventory

`corpus.py inventory` → `Inventory: 612/612 source files, 24 modules, 22
features, 23 variants`

All 612 discovered source files are accounted for. Note that
`sources/feature-inventory.json` carries `summary.total_features: 20` while the
file itself contains **22** feature records and the tool reports 22. The summary
field is stale; the record list is authoritative.

### The source registry, and what it cannot verify

`sources/source-registry.json` holds **101** anchors and is pinned to
`308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437`. Measured on the last
`validate` run: 94 anchors content-hash verified, 0 placeholder, 0 mismatched, 0
naming a missing file; 88 line ranges in bounds, 0 outside, 0 unparseable; 84
plain identifiers checked, 84 present, 0 absent.

Three limits are stated here rather than only in the registry's own `hash_note`
fields:

1. **3 hardware anchors are unverifiable from this repository.**
   `FB2-SRC-HW-000001..000003` name Altium `.SchDoc` files that live in the
   separate `foxBMS2_hw` repository. `content_hash` and `location.file_hash`
   both read `unresolved`; `hash_status` is
   `external_design_file_unverifiable_from_this_repository`. **14 records cite
   them — 10 non-review records and 4 review records** — and those records carry
   the limitation themselves.
2. **4 anchors have no single machine-checkable symbol.** The provenance checker
   records `symbol_unverifiable_prose` for these and cannot verify them by symbol
   match; their content hashes and line ranges *are* verified. They are
   `FB2-SRC-COD-000044` (whole `rtc.c` module body, lines 70–653),
   `FB2-SRC-COD-000076` (the 12-line FreeRTOS markdown README),
   `FB2-SRC-COD-000077` (the whole 114-line `requirements.txt`) and
   `FB2-SRC-COD-000088` (the copyright/licence header of `dp83869.c`, lines
   1–59). Each is legitimately about a whole file, a whole module or a prose
   block, so no identifier can be named without understating the claim.
3. **7 of the 101 anchors name no file in this repository, so their content hash
   cannot be verified here** — and the arithmetic is exact, not approximate:
   **94 verified + 7 without a local file = 101**, with 0 placeholder, 0
   mismatched and 0 naming a missing file.
   - **3** are the external hardware anchors above
     (`content_hash: unresolved`).
   - **4** are documentation anchors (`FB2-SRC-DOC-000001..000004`) that record
     a `url_or_path` and a `section_anchor` into upstream foxBMS documentation
     rather than a path in this tree. Their `location.content_hash` is recorded
     and carried, but there is no local file here to hash, so the checker counts
     them as anchors without a local file rather than as verified. Nothing is
     silently skipped: the tally prints them.

## 9. Gaps and Limitations

1. **No target-hardware evidence.** 0 of 33. The `execution_kind` enum has no
   target-hardware member, so claiming any would require fabricating one. The
   macOS host runs are real product code on a development host and are
   explicitly not credited as target hardware. The repository's four
   `tests/unit-hw/test_tms570_*.c` target-hardware tests were never even
   attempted by the SIL harness.
2. **10 records' hardware provenance rests on an external repository.**
   Anchors `FB2-SRC-HW-000001..000003` name Altium `.SchDoc` files in
   `foxBMS2_hw`, which is present neither in this working tree nor in any commit
   of it; their `content_hash` and `file_hash` both read `unresolved`. 14 records
   cite them — 10 non-review records plus 4 review records. This is also why
   `HWE.2` and `HWE.3` cannot be discharged from here.
3. **4 anchors have no single machine-checkable symbol** (whole-module scope, a
   markdown README, `requirements.txt`, a licence header). Their content hashes
   and line ranges are verified; their symbol occurrence is not, and no symbol
   can be named without understating what each one claims. See §5.
4. **6 synthetic executions record `pass` with no retained evidence.**
   `FB2-VER-EXE-000001`…`000006` (profile `synthetic_reference`) each carry
   `execution_kind: synthetic_fixture`, `outcome: pass`, `logs: []` and no
   evidence file. `docs/artifacts/evidence/synthetic-fixtures/` holds **no fixture
   artefact** — its only file is a hand-written `MANIFEST.md` documenting the gap —
   so the fixture never existed and the `pass` cannot be checked by anyone. That
   `MANIFEST.md` records the gap against `FB2-REV-FND-000143`, **which does not
   exist in the corpus** (42 finding records, numbered to `FB2-REV-FND-000042`), so
   the gap sits in no canonical record.
5. **5 execution records carry a suite-results digest belonging to a `.work`
   scratch file** rather than the evidence file they name.
   `FB2-VER-EXE-000008`…`000012` all carry
   `output_hashes.sil_suite_results_all = sha256:cbbdebeecd54720561753562f7c7dd3ca105e04ca36494f52b674d9fd5a00f67`,
   which resolves to `docs/artifacts/.work/verification-env/sil/logs/RESULTS-POST-fix.json`
   — **gitignored and not in the distribution** — and not to the
   `results-sil-all.json` (`sha256:edd3e70888c75ba075db2dadb17cd9cfb369adfce4b8ac4a05aaefada3c64589`)
   those records cite in their `logs[]`. `FB2-VER-EXE-000015` additionally names
   eight `.work/` paths directly in its `logs[]`. The reproducible command for
   the SIL run is in the **tracked**
   `evidence/actual-runs/foxbms2-sil-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/RUNBOOK.md`.
6. **Link currency is not maintained.** 326 of 489 links carry a stale endpoint
   revision and all 489 are marked `change_suspect_status: false`. See §4.
7. **The pre-SIL host run remains the only evidence for the first five
   failures**, root-caused to untyped `void *` parameters in
   `src/app/engine/database/database.h:209` interacting with the shipped CMock
   configuration. A real product defect, not a harness artefact. No result was
   adjusted to make a test pass. The SIL run adds a separate and worse finding:
   **53 of its 245 green tests assert nothing** (`FB2-REV-FND-000042`).
8. **Automated review coverage 64%** (144/224). **80** distinct artifact IDs are
   uncovered by any review record.
9. **Three applicable processes have no backing artefact of any kind:** `SWE.3`,
   `HWE.3`, `HWE.4`. All three are `gap`, and all three were previously recorded
   `mapped` or `partially_mapped`. **Eighteen more are `partially_mapped`**
   because at least one of their own `expected_artifacts` families has no
   record. Only **4** ASPICE processes are `mapped`. See §3.1.
10. **Human approval 0%.** No human has approved any record.
11. **Production authorization 0%.** Every record is `production_authorized:
    false`, by policy.
12. **`source_grounding` 38%.** 164 of 263 records carry no `source_refs`; these
    are mostly synthetic records with nothing in the pinned source to anchor to.
13. **`render_e2e_html.py --check` exits 1** on 14 `implementation` records that
    have no owning section in the renderer. Tool-side; outside this
    workstream's write boundary. The HTML deliverable itself is regenerated,
    tracked and guard-audited.

Negative-scenario coverage is **closed**: 20/20 mutations implemented, and 20/20
detected by the rule each one declares, 3/3 change lifecycles structurally
complete.

**This dimension is now a measurement, not a count of files.** Until
2026-09-29 `negative_scenario_validation` reported `len(mutation files on disk)`
over a fixed denominator of 20, so it read `20/20` whether the scenarios
detected anything or not — including while the mutation gate was broken and 8 of
the 20 were failing (finding `FB2-REV-FND-000032`). It now executes the
mutation and change-lifecycle scenarios through the same path acceptance gate
`[5/8]` uses and reports how many PASS. `20/20` means twenty scenarios ran and
twenty passed; the figure drops the moment one of them does not. Verified by
temporarily breaking one scenario's declared detector: the dimension read
`19/20` and named `SCN-MUT-005` as the failure. The gate, the rules and the
scenarios are unchanged.

A separate defect of the same class was found in the same pass:
`traceability_integrity` counted its dangling links from whatever findings
happened to be in memory, which was only the validate pass when the caller ran
one. A bare `corpus.py coverage` therefore reported `0 dangling` without having
checked a link. It now re-runs link validation for its own figure.

Five further dimensions are presence checks or declared constants rather than
measurements, and are labelled as such in the generated traceability document
(`docs/artifacts/views/traceability/traceability-document.md`):
`scope_accounting` and `export_reproducibility` (presence),
`semantic_consistency_checks` (declared count), `human_approval` and
`production_authorization` (policy constants, enforced elsewhere by the
`human_approval_rejected` and `production_authorized_rejected` rules and by gate
`[7/8]`), and `standards_mapping`, which measures whether a disposition names a
resolving artefact rather than whether any mapping is satisfied — see §3.1. None
of them keys off a gate, and none is changed here.
